event.title: Canyon Storm
event.summary: At least two bodies have been recovered following a flash flood in the Grand Canyon, with search efforts continuing for over a dozen individuals still missing. The flood, which struck a remote area including Phantom Ranch, has left park officials concerned about the potential for more flooding due to forecasted storms.

timeline.title: Flash Floods in Grand Canyon Result in Two Deaths and One Missing Person
timeline.summary: Over the weekend, flash floods in the Grand Canyon led to the deaths of two individuals, with one person still unaccounted for. Rescue efforts have been complicated by ongoing heavy rains, which are typical during the seasonal monsoon. More than 80 others were rescued, and search teams continue to look for the missing hiker amidst concerns about further flooding.

event_overview.title: About Canyon Storm
event_overview.subject: Canyon Storm
event_overview.summary: Canyon Storm refers to the flash-flood emergency that began when heavy rainfall triggered flooding in the inner Grand Canyon on August 29, 2026. The event centered on Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area, where floodwaters damaged trails, bridges, utilities, and visitor facilities and prompted evacuations and closures managed by Grand Canyon National Park.

facts.label: Start and location
facts.value: The significant flash-flood event began at approximately 2:30 p.m. on August 29, 2026, in Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area of Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona.

facts.label: Responsible public agency
facts.value: Grand Canyon National Park, a unit of the U.S. National Park Service, led response operations in coordination with the Arizona Department of Public Safety; the American Red Cross assisted evacuees on the South Rim.

facts.label: Affected inner-canyon access
facts.value: Closures included Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, the North Kaibab Trail, and the Black and Silver bridges across the Colorado River; NPS said there was no estimated reopening date for the initially closed areas.

facts.label: Infrastructure and water supply
facts.value: The flood extensively damaged inner-canyon infrastructure, including the Transcanyon Waterline that supplies park water, leading the park to impose Stage 4 water restrictions on the South Rim beginning August 31, 2026.

facts.label: Visitor and river operations
facts.value: Nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek were reported destroyed, and the Colorado River was temporarily closed to river traffic because debris and metal structures had entered the river.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the immediate human toll and recovery response from the August 29 flash flood, not every closure, infrastructure repair, weather forecast, or later investigation connected to the event.
